article_notes: 122 shelter dogs in Thailand without clinical signs, screened by smear and PCR for A. platys, B. vogeli and E. canis. Haematology (13 CBC variables) is compared between uninfected dogs and single-, double- and triple-infected dogs (Tables 1-3, Kruskal-Wallis with pairwise tests). No dog had clinical disease and no clinical severity or outcome measure was recorded; the groups are infection status, not severity. Comparisons against uninfected dogs are infected vs healthy (not extracted). The single vs double vs triple infection contrast (no significant differences among infected groups) is co-infection against haematology values, with no severity outcome, so it was not extracted as a severity association. The B. vogeli-only group is small (size not printed in the text; Figure 1 only).
